title: Graceful region ejection and error-budget escrow playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood needs a deterministic, low-risk mechanism to pull a misbehaving region or availability zone out of the serving topology without violating customer SLAs and while preserving high-priority traffic. Current failover is reactive and coarse: regions are drained quickly when error budgets burn, which has caused user-visible failures during past incidents and has no standardized way to re-introduce capacity.

Goal:
Define per-endpoint and per-model SLI metrics, establish an error-budget escrow system, and codify a graceful region ejection and re-introduction playbook that integrates with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies. Deliverables include: SLI definitions (latency/availability/quality), a deterministic error-budget escrow algorithm, region ejection criteria and stepwise rollback, circuit breaker parameter defaults with adaptive scaling, and monitoring/alerting runbooks.

Scope:
- Per-route (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank) SLI definitions for 95/99 latency and availability.
- Model-variant quality SLI for hallucination/regression signals (basic token-level divergence + eval set pass-rate).
- Error-budget escrow: a reserve that can be borrowed for controlled regional evacuation or surge tolerance and a repayment policy.
- Graceful region ejection: staged traffic reweighting, KV-cache redistributions, prioritized tenant preservation, and automatic re-introduction criteria.
- Circuit breaker and load-shedding defaults for single-region and multi-region deployments.
- Observability: dashboards, burn-rate alerts, and postmortem templates.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting serving runtime kernels. We will rely on existing autoscaler and routing APIs.
- Deep model quality metrics beyond lightweight eval hooks (ML team separately owns detailed offline evals).
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLI definitions published in the SLO registry and ingested by our metrics pipeline for all production routes.
A2: Error-budget escrow algorithm implemented as a service-level controller with unit and integration tests, backed by metrics and audit logs.
A3: Playbook for graceful region ejection implemented in the routing layer; can perform phased 10%-50%-90% reweighting with KV-cache redistribution hooks.
A4: Circuit breaker presets and adaptive backoff implemented; default thresholds produce <1% false-positive ejections on historical traffic.
A5: Runbook and dashboards created; at least two oncall engineers validate the incident drill in staging.
A6: Postmortem template updated to include escrow borrow events and region ejection rationale.
design_decisions: D1: Use tenant-weighted error budgeting: error budget burn is calculated both global and per-tenant for high-impact customers; heavier tenants get protection slices to avoid wholesale ejection when only low-priority tenants cause burn.

D2: Error-budget escrow reserve equal to 10% of a route's monthly budget by default. Escrow can be borrowed during bursty periods or to perform graceful ejections, but must be repaid within the next 72 hours or triggers policy enforcement (priority throttles).

D3: Region ejection is treated as a staged reweighting (10/30/60/90) over configurable windows (default 2m/5m/10m/15m) rather than immediate cutover to preserve KV cache hit-rates and to prevent cache thrashing.

D4: Circuit breaker states will be Expanded from traditional Closed/Open/Half-Open to Closed/Degraded/Evicted with explicit reason codes: latency, error-rate, quality-regression, and capacity. Routing will prefer fallbacks before eviction when available.

D5: Load-shedding policy is quality-aware: first shed background/low-priority routes (batch embeddings, low-cost rerank) and then degrade generation output length/temperature for non-critical requests before global rejection.
metrics_and_sli_definitions: SLI: availability_success_rate = successful_responses / total_requests (for a request to count as successful it must return HTTP 200 and not be marked as fallback or degraded). Buckets: 95th percentile per-route per-region and global aggregation.
SLI: p95_latency_ms and p99_latency_ms measured on request processing time end-to-end at the ingress proxy with tags for route, model_variant, region, and priority_tier.

SLI: quality_regression_rate = eval_failure_count / eval_samples over rolling 1h windows using a small, curated prompt set per route (baseline controlled by ModelOps). Thresholds: >2% regressions in 1h triggers quality degradation alert.
SLI: kv_cache_hit_rate = cache_hits / cache_lookups measured per-region; if kv_cache_hit_rate drops >40% during reweighting, slow further ejection steps to allow warm-up.
Error budget accounting: burn rate computed on a 1h and 24h sliding window; borrow allowed from escrow with audit entries showing who/what borrowed and the repayment deadline.
Tenant slice policy: top 5% revenue tenants have isolated mini-escrows that cannot be borrowed by lower-priority tenants.
error_budget_escrow_algorithm: Escrow pool calculation: escrow = floor(0.10 * monthly_error_budget(route)) with an adjustable min/max per route.
Borrow conditions: can borrow from escrow when 1h burn_rate > 3x and immediate ejection would cause >5% customer impact; borrow capped to 50% of escrow per event.
Repayment: controller schedules repayment at linear rate over next 72 hours by tightening non-critical limits and applying temporary throttles to best-effort tenants.
Escrow emergency: if escrow exhausted, trigger automatic priority-based throttles and accelerated ejection window. All borrow events emit audit logs and Slack+PagerDuty alerts.
circuit_breaker_configs: Default preset (per route): Degraded threshold: p95_latency > 1200ms OR error_rate > 1.5% sustained for 3m. Evict threshold: p95_latency > 2s OR error_rate > 5% sustained for 1m.
Adaptive scaling: thresholds multiply by 1.5 during measured burst windows to reduce false positives; tuned by historical-traffic model in telemetry service.
Half-open equivalent: Degraded -> test-traffic slice (2% traffic) to validate before reintroducing higher weights. Test slice is pinned to low-latency models or dedicated capacity when available.
Reason codes must be recorded and surfaced: LATENCY, ERR_RATE, QUALITY, CAPACITY. Each recorded with sample windows and underlying metrics.
failover_playbook: 1) Detection: Automated monitor detects sustained burn (see circuit_breaker_configs). PagerDuty alert is triggered to oncall.

2) Triage (0-5m): Oncall reviews affected regions, tries soft remediation (scale up, reduce request length, enable lightweight caching). If burn persists, controller issues escrow borrow and starts stage 1 reweighting.

3) Stage reweighting (5-30m): 10% traffic shift every configured window; monitor kv_cache_hit_rate and p95_latency. If KV cache drop >40% or error budget increases unexpectedly, pause and warm caches.
4) Prioritized preservation: During reweighting, top-tier tenants are tagged as "protected" and their traffic is routed preferentially; low-priority traffic may be fully shed first.

5) Evicted state (>90% ejection): Mark region as EVICED; routing stops sending new session-affinitive traffic. Annotate region metadata and trigger infra remediation runbook (hardware or network escalation).
6) Reintroduction (post-fix): Start with a test-traffic slice (2-5%) in Degraded state; validate KV cache warm-up and run 30m stability window before staged ramp to 100%.
7) Post-incident: Rabbit hole analysis; if escrow was used, repayment policy executed and postmortem includes borrow justification.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: Per-route SLO summary with global and per-region burn rate, escrow balance, and top offending tenants.
Alerts: burn_rate_warning (1h, 2x), burn_rate_critical (1h, 5x), escrow_low (escrow < 20%), region_kv_drop (delta > 40%), quality_regression (>=2%/1h), and unexpected_reintroduction_failure.
Oncall runbook links and escalation: all shift-based alerts have explicit playbooks and a contact list including ModelOps, Networking, and Customer Success.
rollout_plan: Week 1 (staging): Implement SLI ingestion and escrow controller in staging; run synthetic drills with injected errors across regions.
Week 2 (canary): Enable playbook for a small subset of low-impact routes (internal-only embeddings and rerank). Verify false positive rate <1% over 72h.
Week 3 (gradual): Expand to public chat/generation routes with tenant protection enabled and observe for one 2-week cycle.
Drills: schedule two live drills where we intentionally borrow escrow and perform a controlled region ejection to validate rollbacks and repayment.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Escrow borrowing could be abused by automated jobs or misconfigured alerts. Mitigation: require two-stage approval for borrowing >20% of escrow and rate-limit borrow frequency.
Risk: KV cache thrash during reweighting causing secondary latency spikes. Mitigation: staged reweighting windows and cache-warmup hooks integrated with serving runtime.

Risk: Tenant protection could starve lower-priority customers causing contractual issues. Mitigation: explicit SLA tiers and opt-in for protected slices; Customer Success to notify impacted customers.
post_deployment_checks: All routes have SLI ingestion showing non-empty data within 24 hours.
Escrow controller emits audit logs for every borrow event in the logging cluster and Slack channel #slo-escrow.
Two oncall engineers ran the staging drill and confirmed reintroduction criteria work as expected.
